rule: ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claims 8, 10 and 11: the prototype wins by default and only a real constraint it cannot express overrides it, so the server-paged address book API (repo-addressbook-p3-010, ruling cv-025: page size is server configuration, with no way to ask for a whole category) overrides only the prototype's mechanism of holding every row in the page, while everything that constraint does not force (filter as you type across the whole category, no apply button, a results line counting matches, pagination hidden unless matches run past a page) stays the prototype's, as claim 1 requires the real service to match Design Release 2.1 wherever it can.
outcome: Search on the server, with the prototype's live behaviour on top. The filter stays a GET form to /address-book carrying category, search and type; the address book API filters a whole category by q (the widened fields) and type and returns 8 a page. Without JavaScript, pressing Enter in the search field or choosing a type and pressing Enter submits it. With JavaScript, the page re-requests the list as the user types or changes Type (debounced) and swaps in the table, results line and pagination without a full reload, with no apply button. While filtering, the results line counts the matches and pagination shows only when the matches run past 8. Same locally, in the stub, on the compose stack and in CDP. The prototype's mechanism of loading a category's every address into the page as JSON and filtering in the browser is set aside: the real book is paged on the server and cannot be asked for everything, a persistence and cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express.
